title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
claim: Lacunary tungstate precursors can rearrange into larger all-inorganic building units in which metal octahedra fuse by shared edges, not only by single bridging oxygen atoms.
explanation: Using γ-SiW10, Peng’s frameworks W1-Na and W1-K contain {Cu4Si2W16} clusters made of two {SiW8Cu2O36} fragments. Each fragment is a γ-SiW10 derivative in which one edge-sharing {WO6} pair is replaced by a distorted edge-sharing {CuO6} pair, and the two fragments join through two edge-sharing WO6 and two edge-sharing CuO6 octahedra. The review highlights this as distinct from the conventional shared-oxygen connection.
scope: Copper–silicotungstate all-inorganic frameworks derived from γ-SiW10, namely W1-Na and W1-K.
conditions: Hydrothermal synthesis from the lacunary γ-SiW10 precursor; Na+ or K+ as the framework linker.
caveats: The edge-fused connectivity is established for this {Cu4Si2W16} pair. The review does not claim that every lacunary precursor rearranges in the same way.
